originality.rationale: The same Richardson stability function and its scalar positivity horizon are published and acknowledged as prior work. The new claim is a graph-wide distance criterion with sharp refinement counts 3 and 18, which is not a corollary of scalar decay positivity and was not found in inspected source texts. Residual unindexed equivalent literature remains possible.
residual_risks: A graph-specific theorem under a different terminology (absolute monotonicity, positivity radius, path support) may be unindexed or inaccessible.
Only local-in-step graph positivity is classified, not all positive timesteps or the entire family of refinements above eighteen.
The unusual standard-r=2 graph of diameter three illustrates a sign cancellation, but no exhaustive classification at that boundary is claimed.

value.rationale: The all-size/all-positive-weight diameter criteria are a motivated structural numerical-analysis answer, yielding two sharp microstep design cutoffs (3 and 18) and a subtle failure of usual two-substep extrapolation on a diameter-three diffusion network. It characterizes when arbitrarily small timesteps can restore nonnegative transitions rather than merely giving a numerical negative example.
